title: Disentangled Dual-Granularity Learning for Market-Adaptive Stock Return Forecasting under Non-Stationary Environments

problem.claim: Stock return forecasting requires extracting non-linear patterns from historical stock data.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often use monolithic stock-feature inputs and fixed temporal receptive fields, entangling short-term fluctuations with long-term trends and impeding adaptation to non-stationary environments.

contributions.claim: The authors propose DDGL-Net to decouple and integrate diverse temporal signals.
DDGE isolates fine-grained short-term and coarse-grained long-term features through parallel streams.
MACM dynamically reweights granularity contributions using global market context, while HR-MoE decomposes forecasts into stable consensus and adaptive residuals.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show DDGL-Net outperforming state-of-the-art baselines on real-world stock datasets.
The authors report that the experiments validate disentangled modeling and regime-aware adaptation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning is used to extract non-linear patterns for stock return forecasting.
Monolithic inputs and fixed temporal fields entangle short-term and long-term signals, limiting adaptation.
DDGL-Net addresses the gap through dual-granularity disentanglement and integration.
MACM applies market-contextual reweighting and HR-MoE models stable and adaptive forecast components.
The authors report superior baseline performance on real-world stock datasets.
